item.title: Cypress Ranch, Lake Creek advance to UIL volleyball state championships
item.description: Cypress Ranch will take on Allen at the UIL state championships. (Raquel Natalicchio/Houston Chronicle) Facing a two-set deficit Saturday evening at Delmar Fieldhouse, the Cypress Ranch volleyball team rallied to beat Austin Lake Travis 21-25, 22-25, 25-18, 25-21, 15-9 and secure the program's first state championship appearance. The Mustangs (40-7), who have won 29 consecutive matches, will face Allen (42-2) for the UIL Class 6A Division I title at 6 p.m. next Saturday at the Curtis Culwell Center in Garland. Lake Travis swept Cy Ranch in their first meeting at the Leander Volleypolooza tournament in August, and it looked like the rematch might be headed in the same direction. But the Mustangs, led by coach Collea McKinney, were able to swing the momentum back in their favor and win three consecutive sets to clinch their spot in the final. Regional champions for a second consecutive season, Cy Ranch will face an Allen team that is riding a 20-match winning streak of its own. The Eagles will be making their first state championship appearance since 2003 after sweeping Duncanville in the other semifinal match Saturday at the Thomas Coliseum in Haltom City. Cy Ranch is one of two Houston-area teams headed to state. The other is Lake Creek, which earned its spot in the Class 5A Division II final with a 25-20, 25-14, 25-20 win over New Braunfels at the Merrell Center in Katy. The Lions (43-10) have won 10 consecutive matches and will also be making their first championship match appearance. Lake Creek reached the semifinals in 2022 before losing to eventual champion Colleyville Heritage. Lake Creek, led by coach Kayli Kane, has swept four of its five playoff opponents and will play Abilene Wylie (39-4) for the state title at 11 a.m. next Saturday in Garland. Wylie swept Colleyville Heritage in the other semifinal matchup. The Bulldogs won the Class 3A state title in 2013 and are making their first championship appearance as a 5A program. Tompkins was denied a spot in the Class 6A Division II final with a 25-16, 23-25, 22-25, 25-21, 15-11 loss to Austin Westlake in the earlier semifinal match at Delmar Fieldhouse. The Falcons (32-8) rallied from two sets down to beat Fulshear in the regional final earlier this week, giving coach Allison Merrell her 400th career victory. Tompkins was making its first state semifinals appearance since 2022 after losing in the regional final last year. Columbus also saw its season come to a close with a 25-17, 25-13, 25-18 loss to defending state champion Goliad in the Class 3A Division I semifinals Saturday at Waco Midway High School. item.title: The 2026 CIAC girls soccer tournament quarterfinals are complete. What you need to know
item.description: East Hampton's Olivia Correia looks for an open teammate in front of Daniel Hand's Molly Mcgetrick during a CIAC high school girls soccer game at East Hampton High School in East Hampton, Conn., Friday, November 13, 2026. (Dave Zajac/Hearst Connecticut Media) The second round of the CIAC girls soccer tournaments was held Tuesday. Here is the full schedule and scoreboard for the tournaments. Here is what you need to know. Reigning CIAC girls soccer champions eliminated No team is still alive with a chance to defend its CIAC championship. All were eliminated before the semifinal round. Greenwich, the No. 4 seed in Class LL, lost in the quarterfinals Friday at home to No. 5 Notre Dame Prep. On Saturday, No. 2 Pomperaug shut out No. 7 Masuk in the Class L quarterfinals. Greenwich and Masuk each won their first state championship last year. So did Foran in Class M. The Lions were eliminated in the second round by RHAM. Morgan also lost in the second round in Class S. All four teams were first-time champions. Two of last year's finalists also did not return: Amity (LL) and Northwest Catholic (M, failed to make the playoffs). North Haven (L) and Old Saybrook (S) are still alive. It's a return of some of the usual suspects in the semifinals this coming week. No double-digit seeds remain in CIAC girls soccer tournament There are no Cinderella seeds left in the draw. It's a point getting repeated over and over, but part of the intent of the new tournament seeding system was the teams that play the better schedules would get lower seeds. The highest seed still alive among the 16 remaining teams is RHAM at No. 7 in Class M. All of the top seeds, all of the No. 3 seeds, three of the No. 2 seeds and three No. 5 seeds remain. Only one No. 4 seed advanced. There were four double-digit seeds in last year's semifinals. This system is on a one-year trial basis. There could be some things tweaked. The hope is teams will go out and schedule non-conference games when able to. The intention was for the lower seeded teams to go deeper, like it has happened in girls lacrosse. One suggestion if possible: try to avoid conference matchups in the early rounds. Sign up for the Connecticut Briefing from CT Insider. "Well, I think we probably did Ireland a favour today," the 62-year-old said. "Let me put it that way, because I think Ireland deep down know that if they play like that against South Africa, they're gonna be up against it." "They would have taken another scrum and another scrum and another scrum, and they wouldn't have worried about the ref making a call about collapsing or early engaging. item.title: Sabalenka apologises & says viral comment 'not directed at Svitolina'
item.description: Aryna Sabalenka will be replaced as world number two by Mirra Andreeva on Monday [Getty Images] Aryna Sabalenka has apologised and denied claims that she insulted opponent Elina Svitolina after a viral clip showed her swearing during her WTA Finals defeat by the Ukrainian. A video of world number two Sabalenka angrily gesturing and swearing in Russian during her 6-3 3-6 6-1 defeat by Ukraine's Svitolina was posted on social media on Saturday. Some commentators interpreted Belarusian Sabalenka's comments as an insult towards Svitolina or Ukrainians in general. Sabalenka later wrote on social media that "my comment was not directed at Elina" but she lost her temper because of the behaviour of some fans. "I was frustrated with a small group of spectators who were aggressively cheering my mistakes, and I reacted emotionally in the moment," the 28-year-old wrote. "That said, I should have handled my frustration differently, and I apologise to anyone offended." Sabalenka said Svitolina had played a great match, adding that she wished her "all the best for the rest of the tournament". Ukrainian players have a long-standing policy of not shaking hands with Russian or Belarusian players because of the ongoing invasion of their country. Some commentators interpreted Belarusian Sabalenka's comments as an insult towards Svitolina or Ukrainians in general. Sabalenka later wrote on social media that "my comment was not directed at Elina" but she lost her temper because of the behaviour of some fans. "I was frustrated with a small group of spectators who were aggressively cheering my mistakes, and I reacted emotionally in the moment," the 28-year-old wrote. "That said, I should have handled my frustration differently, and I apologise to anyone offended." Sabalenka said Svitolina had played a great match, adding that she wished her "all the best for the rest of the tournament". Ukrainian players have a long-standing policy of not shaking hands with Russian or Belarusian players because of the ongoing invasion of their country. They also do not take pre-match photographs with each other. item.title: Svitolina races into WTA Finals showpiece against Andreeva
item.description: Elina Svitolina is a three-time finalist at the WTA Finals [Getty Images] Elina Svitolina dropped just three games as she thrashed Linda Noskova to set up a WTA Finals showpiece against Mirra Andreeva. Ukraine's Svitolina was composed and aggressive in a 6-2 6-1 victory over Wimbledon champion Noskova in just 64 minutes. It caps a remarkable turnaround for world number six Svitolina in Indian Wells, having suffered a heavy defeat in her opening group match against Andreeva. However, she has shown all of her fighting spirit to win her next three matches, including snapping a six-match losing streak to Aryna Sabalenka on Friday. Svitolina now has 11 wins over top-10 opponents this year - the most of any player on the WTA Tour. "After losing the first match I was ready to go home, and now I'm in the final," the 32-year-old said. "I will do my homework with my coaches - I will try to win a bit more games than I did in the first match [against Andreeva]." Svitolina is back in the world's top 10 for the first time since October 2021. She took maternity leave in May 2022 to have daughter Skai, and has made an effort to play more aggressive tennis since her return. She returned brilliantly against Noskova, neutralising the Czech's big serve from the first game. Noskova was well below her best, hitting 11 double faults and committing 27 unforced errors to Svitolina's 18. It is the third time Svitolina has reached the final of the season-ending tournament, having lifted the trophy in 2018. Earlier, Andreeva became the youngest player for 22 years to reach the WTA Finals showpiece with a composed victory over Jessica Pegula. French Open champion Andreeva came back from a break down in both sets to win 6-3 6-4. The 19-year-old Russian is the youngest finalist at the season-ending event since Maria Sharapova, who was 17 when she won the title in 2004. Victory over American Pegula ensures Andreeva will finish the year as world number two. "I did not feel one bit of pressure today, I don't know why," Andreeva told Sky Sports. "Usually I feel like on these important points or when I have to close out the match or the set I get so tight. "But for some reason today I was just playing. I was just not thinking about anything, just trying to enjoy." Tournament debutant Andreeva has yet to drop a set and has not lost more than four games in any of her eight sets. The 18 games she has lost is the fewest for a finalist at the WTA Finals since the round-robin format was introduced in 2003. Under the guidance of coach Conchita Martinez, Andreeva has developed her serve into a real weapon. She won 77% of points behind her first serve and hit 17 winners to outmuscle Pegula. Andreeva also showed impressive composure, remaining unfazed despite going an early break down in both sets against the home favourite. item.description: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 14: Stephen Thompson holds his gloves as he announces his retirement following his victory over Charles Radtke in their welterweight fight during the UFC 334 event at Madison Square Garden on November 14, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Jeff Bottari/Zuffa LLC) Zuffa LLC Most UFC retirement fights wind up confirming that it was time for the longtime fighter to walk away from the Octagon. Sometimes, and it is rare, the tenured star gets a victory in their final fight. Almost never have we seen a future Hall of Famer go out the way Stephen “Wonderboy” Thompson did on Saturday night at UFC 334. In signature fashion, Thompson defeated Charles Radtke with a spinning wheel kick in the third round. The MMA universe flooded social media to react to the perfect ending to an excellent career. Let’s talk UFC. Wonderboy Thompson vs. Charles Radtke Key Facts Detail Info Event UFC 334 Date Nov. 14, 2026 Venue Madison Square Garden, New York Weight class Welterweight Result Thompson def. item.title: AEW Full Gear 2026 Results As The Kasper Brothers Make Surprise Debut
item.description: AEW Full Gear 2026 Graphic All Elite Wrestling AEW has welcomed several notable former WWE stars in recent months, but Tony Khan and company had another surprise up their sleeves at Full Gear. This time, it was the arrival of the Kasper Brothers, formerly known as Julius and Brutus Creed in WWE. In the second match of AEW Full Gear’s main card, The Young Bucks defeated Mark Davis and Jake Doyle to retain the AEW World Tag Team Championship. The Motor City Machine Guns, the new No. 1 contenders after defeating FTR in a best-of-five series, came down to the ring to greet the champions, seemingly setting up their upcoming title match. However, an alarm sounded, and a logo for the “Kasper Brothers” appeared on the video screens inside the Mortgage Matchup Center. The moment left fans and even the wrestlers in the ring confused until the former Julius and Brutus Creed emerged on the stage. Previously known by those names in WWE, the brothers are now going by their real names, Jacob and Drew Kasper, respectively. They marched to the ring to confront the Motor City Machine Guns and The Young Bucks before FTR arrived and joined them in an attack on the babyfaces. It was one of AEW’s bigger surprise debuts in recent months. While Creed, Kingston and Dragunov were all notable additions, their arrivals had been heavily rumored before they officially debuted. Earlier this month, Fightful Select reported that the Kaspers had mutually agreed to leave WWE, where Jacob had been since 2020 and Drew since 2021. Both were collegiate wrestlers who transitioned to professional wrestling, beginning their careers in NXT before moving to WWE’s main roster in 2023. The Kasper Brothers were best known for their alliance with Ivy Nile and, later, Chad Gable as part of American Made. However, the group’s run together was relatively short-lived due to Gable’s absence with an injury. The brothers also played a role in the No Disqualification match between the two El Grande Americanos at Noche de Los Grandes in May. The Kaspers eventually returned to NXT in September, where they remained until their final match on Oct. 20 against Hank and Tank in the quarterfinals of the Dusty Rhodes Tag Team Classic. Their contracts expired shortly afterward, on Nov. 6. Long considered a tag team with potential, the Kaspers now have a chance to establish themselves in AEW’s red-hot tag team division alongside the likes of The Young Bucks, the Motor City Machine Guns, New Level and FTR. As one of the youngest duos in the division, they have plenty of room to grow in a new environment that could provide significant opportunities for both brothers. This article was originally published on Forbes.com

item.title: Explosive offensive, chunk plays push Oregon football past Michigan
item.description: The No. 16 Oregon football team set several season bests, and not just defensively, in a 31-7 demolition of Michigan Nov. 14 at Autzen Stadium. The Ducks (7-3, 5-2 Big Ten) became the first team to hit 30 points against one of the top defensive units in the country Saturday, weeks after an embarrassing offensive showing against a mediocre-at-best Illinois defense . Quarterback Dylan Raiola, benched in a loss to UCLA in early October , passed for 341 yards, the most the Wolverines (5-5, 2-5) have given up all season. Oregon finished with 10 chunk plays - run plays for 10 or more yards or pass plays of 15 or more. "I think its complementary football," coach Dan Lanning said. "When you’re running the ball effectively … I felt like we were able to stay again on pace. We felt like some of the play action game would be a weapon for us early, with the ability to set up some of the runs and then be able to keep your eyes downfield with pocket presence. I thought Dylan did a great job of that. It means you have to have clean pockets to do it." Raiola was particularly effective with his deep ball in the first half, completing 6 of 8 pass attempts longer than 15 yards for 212 yards, including long TDs to Jeremiah McClellan and Dakorien Moore. The wide receiver duo both eclipsed 100 yards for the game, with McClellan catching four passes for 105 yards and a score and Moore hauling in seven passes for 101 yards on nine targets. The most important thing for Oregon heading into the game, however, started with a Thursday meeting between Lanning and Raiola. item.title: GAME THREAD: Cougs play host to Colorado State
item.description: San Diego, California - October 31: Owen Eshelman #17 and Nick Bakken #77 of Washington State celebrate after a touchdown against San Diego State during their game at Snapdragon Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, 2026 in San Diego, California. (Photo by Meg McLaughlin / The San Diego Union-Tribune via Getty Images) Good evening, Cougar football fans. Tonight, your 1-8 Washington State Cougars return back home to host the 3-6 Colorado State Rams. Following a bye week, WSU is back in action and still looking for their first Pac-12 win and first win over an FBS opponent. Of the three games remaining, this one may be their best shot at it. When we last saw the Cougs, they were in rainy San Diego playing the San Diego State Aztecs. The Cougs fought back in that game and even gave themselves a shot at a game-winning drive in the game’s final minutes, but they ultimately never crossed midfield, losing 26-20. As for Colorado State, they lost last week to Boise State 64-38. The 64 points allowed isn’t even the most the Rams have allowed this season. The worst defense by almost every metric in FBS football surrendered 66 to Texas State earlier in the year. They’ve given up 50+ four times in their nine games played. What they lack in defense, they make up for in offense. The Rams are 26th in points per game, 34th in yards per game and rank highly in most offensive advanced metrics. For a more visual image of the disparity between how great Colorado State’s offense is versus how bad their defense is, our great friends from Podcast vs. Everyone showed a spider chart of the Ram offense and defense in their preview episode this week. You may have to squint, but yes, I can assure you that CSU’s defensive metrics are in that chart on the right. This puts the pressure on WSU’s offense to generate some sustained success for really the first time this Pac-12 season. If WSU is going to win their first Pac-12 game this season, they are going to have to score more than they have against any Pac-12 opponent so far. And this is the defense to finally find their groove on. They’ve allowed everything and anything. Not only do they have to find it because the defense is bad, but also because CSU is going to score. They have a prolific offense, and the Cougar defense hasn’t been as sharp in recent weeks. WSU is likely going to have to score at least four to five touchdowns to be in this one. It’s WSU’s first true Pac-12 After Dark game of the season, with kickoff at 7:30 p.m and televised on CBS Sports Network. Go Cougs!

item.title: Recap: Boston College completes the sweep of UMass, 4-2
item.description: BOSTON, MASSACHUSETTS - MARCH 20: Tristan Fraser #10 of the UConn Huskies (not pictured) shoots the puck off the skate of Lukas Gustafsson #8 of the Boston College Eagles for the overtime winning goal behind Louka Cloutier #1 during NCAA men's hockey in the Hockey East Championship semifinal at TD Garden on March 20, 2026 in Boston, Massachusetts. The Huskies won 4-3 in overtime. (Photo by Richard T Gagnon/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Saturday night, the Boston College men’s hockey team hosted the second night of a weekend series against local rival UMass. BC won their game on Friday night, 3-1, in Amherst. Looking for a series sweep, the Eagles also were bringing back top forward Oscar Hemming after he was out with an injury. Boston College picked up right where they left off the previous night. Just under three minutes into the game, BC’s Casey Mutryn slipped a puck by UMass goalie Ethan Eskit for an early 1-0 lead. But from there the play was more even and BC’s offense struggled to generate shots against the rigid Minuteman defense. Then on the other side, UMass went on a long stretch of offensive zone time that was tiring out the Eagles defense. Louka Cloutier kept his team in it with a few clutch saves, but the defense was being pushed to the brink. Eventually BC went on the powerplay and relieved the pressure. But the effort wasn't enough for a big upset win as the Flames , a 21-point favorite, pulled off a 28-23 home victory and clinched a spot in the CUSA title game. item.title: Sabalenka sorry for outburst in Svitolina defeat
item.description: Aryna Sabalenka said an on-court outburst during her WTA Finals loss to Elina Svitolina was directed at "aggressive" fans and not her Ukrainian opponent (Katelyn Mulcahy) Aryna Sabalenka apologized on Saturday after an on-court outburst during her defeat to Ukrainian rival Elina Svitolina at the WTA Finals in Indian Wells. Footage shared widely on social media appeared to show the former world number one swearing in a tirade that some commenters interpreted as directed towards Svitolina or Ukrainians in general. However, Sabalenka said Saturday that she lost her cool due to the behavior of spectators during Friday's 3-6, 6-3, 1-6 defeat, which sent the four-time Grand Slam-winner crashing out. "I want to clarify something from my recent match that has been circulating online," Sabalenka wrote in a post on Instagram. "My comment was not directed at Elina. I was frustrated with a small group of spectators who were aggressively cheering my mistakes and I reacted emotionally in the moment. "That said, I should have handled my frustration differently and I apologise to anyone I offended. Elina played a great match, and I wish her all the best for the rest of the tournament." Svitolina, who has refused to shake hands with tennis players from Russia and its regional ally Belarus since Moscow's invasion of Ukraine in 2022, acknowledged that a match against Sabalenka could carry extra weight for her fans. "As we see there's many, many Ukrainians, many, many flags ... and of course they want me to win this particular match," she said Saturday when asked about Sabalenka's statement. "We've played many times with Aryna ... she has her fans. I have my fans," added Svitolina, who reached the Finals title match with a win over Linda Noskova on Saturday. "I have seen the glimpse of it because obviously it's in the social media," she said. "(I) just hope the matches between us (are) respected. Sometimes in some matches that we've played also there have been not great comments towards me in regards of the war. "It is like this in the social media sometimes the things are turned around a little bit." rcw/bb

item.title: Two Players Punished by NFL Over Los Angeles Rams Game
item.description: Sean McVay and the Rams got the NFL's final decision on Emmanuel Forbes. Getty The Los Angeles Rams saw cornerback Emmanuel Forbes swept up in the NFL’s weekly review process. Forbes received a $10,839 fine for “unnecessary roughness” over “striking/kicking/kneeing” in Week 9 against the Washington Commanders. Officials flagged Forbes for the infraction during the contest, making the ruling less surprising than some other instances around the NFL. The NFL confirmed the anticipated decision in their weekly update. The incident occurred during the second quarter on a first-and-10 from the Commanders 18-yard line. Commanders running back Austin Ekeler gained 7 yards on a carry, and Rams defensive lineman Ty Hamilton received credit for the stop. However, officials flagged Forbes for “unnecessary roughness” over a post-play altercation with Commanders wide receiver Jaden Bradley. The NFL did not fine Bradley over the interaction. Forbes’ fine is less than what the NFL lists as the standard amount for first-time offenses, which this is for the former Commanders first-round draft pick. The NFL could have docked Forbes up to $12,537 for this infraction. A second offense can incur a fine as high as $18,507, which is what Forbes is now subject to if he logs another such infraction. It was an admittedly emotional contest for Forbes. “I had this one circled. Just motivated to play them guys. They let me go to years ago, and just ready to go out there and show myself, what I got,” Forbes told reporters on November 8. “I’m a ball player. And I when I’m playing my best, I think I’m the best in the world.” Rams head coach Sean McVay praised the 2024 waiver claim, who is heading for free agency this offseason. He said Forbes played “great” and commended his ability to overcome a different penalty. “I thought he played tough, I thought he came up in run support, I thought he was sticky in coverage,” McVay told reporters after the game. “I was really proud of Emanuel Forbes. He did a good job today.” NFL Fines Rams’ Emmanuel Forbes, Commanders Player No other Rams players received fines besides Forbes. The NFL did, however, dock Commanders safety Quan Martin $17,911 for a “hit on a defenseless player.” In the second quarter on a third-and-2 from the Texans 28-yard line. Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford’s pass attempt to Tutu Atwell fell incomplete, with no other ruling coming from the in-game officials. Martin came flying in to ensure the incompletion, but with too much vigor for the situation. Players can appeal fines. If this sticks for Martin, he now has his first of three strikes before triggering a one-game suspension under revised league rules announced in August . Over the last three games, all wins for Oregon, Raiola has completed 67% of his passes for 934 yards, nine touchdowns, and zero interceptions. On Saturday, he statistically had his best day of the year, going 20-for-28 with 341 yards, four TDs, and zero INTs. More important than the numbers, though, is that he's playing cleanly and not putting the ball in jeopardy. We didn't see that a week ago, when Ohio State dropped a pair of interceptions that could have swung the momentum of the game. There was one pass against Michigan that you could argue could have been intercepted, but it would have been an incredible play by the defense, which ultimately was not made. After missing six games due to a broken foot, wide receiver Jeremiah McClellan made his return to the field last week against the Ohio State Buckeyes. It wasn't until this game against Michigan, though, that you could say "J-Mac is back." He finished the day with four catches for 105 yards, his first of which went for the game-opening touchdown that lit Autzen Stadium on fire. Moore and McClellan dominated the day for the Ducks, but don't let that make you forget what other players lay lurking among this pass-catching group. TE Jamari Johnson had three catches for 35 yards; Evan Stewart had one catch for 38 yards; and Jalen Lott had one catch for four yards. Oregon's receivers appear to be healthy at long last, and the passing game is benefiting from it. He is now up to 9.5 sacks on the year, which is one shy of his career-high in 2024, and two shy of the Oregon Ducks' program record, set by Nick Reed at 29.5 during his time from 2005-2008. Going into his final two regular-season games, Uiagalelei's number is 28.0. "Obviously, you know, that's not the main focus," Uiagalelei said after the game. "The focus is getting wins. item.description: Former Detroit Lions tight end James Mitchell joined the Dallas Cowboys active roster Saturday night for Week 10. Getty Former Detroit Lions tight end James Mitchell has played two games this season for the Dallas Cowboys. In Week 10, though, the veteran will join the Cowboys active roster for the first time. Dallascowboys.com’s Tommy Yarrish reported Saturday the team signed Mitchell to the active roster as part of a slew of roster moves before Week 10. Dallas signed Mitchell to the 53-man roster from the team’s practice squad. The Lions selected Mitchell on Day 3 of the 2022 NFL Draft. The tight end appeared in 30 games for Detroit, starting one of them during the 2023 campaign. This season, Mitchell has appeared in two games as a practice squad elevation for the Cowboys. He has yet to catch a pass. Cowboys Sign Ex-Lions TE James Mitchell The Lions selected Mitchell at No. 177 overall in the fifth round of the 2022 NFL Draft. The tight end made his NFL debut during Week 4 of his rookie campaign. Mitchell caught all 11 of his targets as a rookie for 113 yards. Those remain career bests for the tight end, who also scored a touchdown as a first-year player. Mitchell started his lone game with the Lions during Week 18 of the 2023 campaign. He caught one pass for 24 yards in that contest. After three seasons with the Lions, Mitchell played with the Carolina Panthers last season. He appeared in five contests with the Panthers. Mandatory Credit: Joseph Maiorana-Imagn Images Breaking Records This week, Ohio State officially launched its campaign for Jeremiah Smith to win this year’s Heisman Trophy. No player has been more productive than Smith over a three-year period, let alone in his first three seasons in college. Finally, A Little Help While there were some major blunders by the Buckeyes, like a ball bouncing off Chris Henry Jr. ’s head resulting in an interception, or Henry dropping what would have been a walk-in touchdown, or the insanely unlucky muffed punt, Smith and the offense looked better. Luke Fahey had a wide range of plays on the day. On one hand, that drop by Henry was perhaps Fahey’s best-placed pass in his young career. On the other, he bounced a ball seven yards in front of his man while scrambling on a third down. He was alright on the day, completing 21 of 31 passes for 201 yards and three touchdowns. There were ups and downs, but he’s getting better. Perhaps the best complement to Smith is a competent run game. Against Northwestern, it finally showed up. Bo Jackson led the way with 114 yards and a touchdown on 20 carries, his ninth career 100-yard game. Isaiah West was also solid with 45 yards on 10 carries while adding a touchdown reception. All in all, it was Ohio State’s fourth-best rushing day of the season and third-best in Big Ten play. If it can continue that over the next two weeks, opening things up with downfield bombs to Smith should help this offense tremendously. Of course, “if” is the biggest word in sports. First, it was a pretty dominant performance by the defensive front against a Northwestern offensive line that nobody would claim to be among the best in the Big Ten. Coming off the bench, Kenyatta Jackson Jr. flashed what many thought he could be this year with a pair of sacks. Alabama transfers James Smith and Qua Russaw each added a sack in the second half, as did Will Smith Jr. Additionally, the defense stood tall a few times, holding Northwestern to field goal attempts as well as responding well after a muffed punt after a three-and-out. All in all, the unit did fine. However, if Northwestern had a healthy Aidan Chiles, this write-up may be more of a postmortem. Overall, the Wildcats earned 15 first downs and converted on six of 15 third downs. An area where the Buckeyes did well was in limiting explosive plays. Northwestern had six passing big plays (of 15+ yards) and one rushing big play (of 10+ yards). Given, three of those passes – for 17, 18, and 41 yards – came on the final drive of the game, capped off by a buzzer-beater “Chris Paul hits a three to cut the lead to 42” kind of touchdown. While limiting a Northwestern team that came into the game averaging 190.2 yards per game and 4.9 yards per carry to a total of 53 yards and 1.8 yards per carry is impressive, it’s still Northwestern. Do that over the next two weeks and we can be impressed. The Last Word Ohio State is a flawed team. Who would have thought losing a Heisman Finalist on offense would result in some hiccups? Of course, that doesn’t explain or excuse the defense’s performance this year. At the same time, who would have thought losing four first-round picks on defense would result in a little regression? Ohio State is flawed, but still alive. It likely isn’t a team good enough to compete for and win a national championship (barring a turnaround that would make the 2024 run blush). But the name of the game is to survive and advance. The Buckeyes are in one-game seasons from here on out. They’re 1-0 today, but need to be 1-0 again in seven days. The path to the CFP is there; it’s thin, bumpy, and lined with all kinds of enemies and traps, but it’s there. Ohio State has to take care of what it can and beat Nebraska in Lincoln next week, and then follow that up with a second win over Michigan in as many years. Maybe getting Smith 20 targets could help? Remember that tracker we had going looking at Smith’s 2026 vs. DeVonta Smith’s 2020 Heisman season? Through 10 games, Jeremiah Smith has 80 receptions for 1,314 yards and 15 touchdowns. DeVonta Smith had 83 receptions for 1,327 yards and 15 touchdowns at this point. And that was on a schedule that may or may not have been affected by defensive backs coming down with COVID and missing time. item.description: Maiden title crowns Novorizontino's Série B campaign The league phase of the 2026 Brazilian Série B Championship came to an end this Saturday (14), with Novorizontino celebrating in Criciúma, Santa Catarina. Tigre do Vale defeated the hosts 1–0 at the Heriberto Hülse Stadium, thanks to a goal from Juninho, securing their first-ever title and promotion to Série A. CBF competitions marketing director Cláudio Gomes highlighted the success of this edition of the competition, which featured fierce contests and the introduction of a new format. “Another Série B successfully delivered. This time, a different Série B, with a new format and playoffs. The final round was full of excitement right up to the last minute. Congratulations to Novorizontino, first-time champions. Congratulations to Juventude on their promotion, too. It is incredibly satisfying to be part of this. It is a great pleasure for the CBF to deliver another outstanding competition,” he said. Cláudio Gomes represented the CBF on the Série B podium Credits: Leo Piva/CBF The competition’s new format kept the race for promotion to the top flight of Brazilian football open until the final round. Unlike previous editions, when the top four teams secured automatic promotion to Série A, starting this season only the champions and runners-up go up automatically. Novorizontino and Juventude claimed those two spots. The other two places will be decided through playoffs, with third facing sixth and fourth facing fifth over two legs. The matchups will be Vila Nova vs Atlético-GO and Fortaleza vs Criciúma. The final round also confirmed the four clubs relegated to Série C: Avaí, Londrina, América-MG and Ponte Preta. item.title: Portugal did the extraordinary with Cristiano Ronaldo. Can they do it without him?
item.description: The captain, the talisman, the brand: former teammates and experts discuss Portugal entering a new era after 23 years There are days football fans hope will never come. For Portugal, this is one of them. For 23 years, Cristiano Ronaldo has been more than the country’s greatest footballer; he has been its defining sporting figure, a symbol of national pride and constant presence in the lives of supporters. After 234 appearances and 146 goals, the No 7 brought that chapter to a close and on Saturday night the team will play their first game without him . The national side are losing more than a great footballer; they are also losing one of the world’s biggest brands. Daniel Sá, the executive director of the Portuguese institute of marketing administration, believes Portugal require reinvention to attract at least some of the millions of viewers who tuned in because of CR7. item.title: Football Daily | Taking a brief minute to remember Pierre Sage’s impact at Crystal Palace
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! So farewell then, Pierre Sage . Many coaches leave under a cloud, not many have their departures completely obscured by the foul, retch-inducing one emanating from another team’s managerial circus, but such was Sage’s fate . The news section of Crystal Palace’s website helpfully tells you the amount of time it might take you to read each story it links through to. For example it should take four minutes or so to get through Tuesday’s “On this day: five big Crystal Palace birthdays”. “England: I love a knee slide!” will take you five. “Prize draw: be a mascot for our next [Bigger Vase] tie!” is a two-minute job. The statement informing the world of Sage’s exit? One minute. Eighty-three words. By way of illustration, the word “words” was the 84th of this paragraph. Just because the man’s French doesn’t mean his exit should be marked with a shrug. As I have been away at a conference, giving a presentation that the MC described as ‘sobering’, I’ve missed the last few days of football, so I was very sad to read about the passing of the great Danny Kelly . Others are far better placed to give tributes to the great man, but for younger generations who can’t comprehend the football cultural significance, Baker and Kelly represented the peak of football phone-ins. Before it became people ranting and raving about wanting the manager sacked as they’ve lost a few games or wanting the club to spend another few hundred million pounds on yet more players, it was about football supporters and supporting, from fans who actually went to games. Their peak was on BBC Radio in the 1990s, and there are too many examples of their greatness, but if I had to pick one, just one to illustrate it, it would, of course, be Gordon the Dundee United supporter and his bow tie . Rest in Peace, Danny Kelly. You gave us such joy” – Noble Francis. As they no longer seem to be ‘Dr Tottenham’, I was wondering if they had maybe passed the soubriquet on. I think the England cricket team has provided the answer (again)” – Andrew Parker. item.title: The beautiful game: revived art prize gives football its creative due once more | Emma John
item.description: Football and the art world have long remained distant but the breadth of entries for this year’s award reveals a healthy revival It may be the Beautiful Game, but in its early decades football was a rare subject for artists. The Italian Futurist Umberto Boccioni whirled an athlete’s body into a vortex of movement in his 1913 painting Dynamism of a Soccer Player . You can see one of the earliest fine art depictions of a match – a smoggy, factory-adjactent scene called Any Wintry Afternoon in England – at the Manchester Art Gallery. If 1930s abstraction is more your thing, you can enjoy decoding the geometric shapes in Kazimir Malevich’s Painterly Realism of a Football Player – Color Masses in the 4th Dimension. I’m guessing the small green pea shape is a ball. These, in any case, were exceptions. In 1953 the Football Assocition launched an art prize, backed by the newly formed Arts Council: the winning works included Going To The Match by LS Lowry, with its crowds flocking to Bolton Wanderers’ then home ground, Burnden Park. An exhibition of the submissions, Football and The Fine Arts, toured the country and the Football Association secretary, Sir Stanley Rous, said he hoped it would finally break the barrier between those two worlds. item.title: Manchester City’s weaknesses under Enzo Maresca are being exposed
item.description: After three straight defeats, City’s manager says he will use the international break to reassess. Their problems may go beyond tactics Sign up for our free newsletter here Enzo Maresca seemed, if not quite baffled by his side’s Saturday defeat to Nottingham Forest, then at least a little put out. After seven straight wins from the start of the season, that’s now three straight defeats, a pattern so unusual that it’s been recorded only once before in top-flight English history, by Sheffield Wednesday in 1904-05. The three defeats were all different, Maresca said, although in all of them City had had more possession and more chances. In the 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa two weeks ago, City had 63% of the ball and had 15 chances to Villa’s eight. In the 1-0 home defeat to Brighton last weekend, they had 62% possession and 21 chances to seven. At the City Ground, it was 79% possession and 12 chances to 11. So Maresca is right in one way: City could look at basic statistics and say they had been unfortunate – although Forest could equally point to the fact that they went into that game third top of the expected goals table but second-bottom of the actual table. item.title: That’s a Mora: Rodrigo and Roma rise with Lazio to give Eternal City new life | Nicky Bandini
item.description: Roma and Lazio have both made unbeaten starts to the Serie A season, giving those in the Italian capital dreams of a Scudetto After nine games in 28 days, Gian Piero Gasperini finally got a moment to pause and reflect on Sunday night. The Roma manager was back in Liguria, where he worked for the best part of a decade across two stints at Genoa, to collect an award from Stelle Nello Sport – an association formed to promote sport in the region – celebrating his career achievements and commitment to courageous attacking football. The timing worked out well. Gasperini’s Roma thumped Sassuolo 3-0 on Saturday, bouncing back from a midweek defeat against Manchester United . That result meant the Giallorossi had scored 31 times in 11 Serie A games. In the past 65 years only two Italian teams – the Juventus and Napoli sides of 2017-18 – had made a more prolific start to a top-flight campaign. More importantly, Roma’s victory meant they remained undefeated in domestic competition this season. Just like their neighbours Lazio, who drew 1-1 away against Napoli in the early kick-off on Sunday. Continue reading...

item.title: Football comes together across Spain to honour Jesús de Miguel: ‘We’ve seen how fragile life is’
item.description: Across La Liga and beyond this weekend, footballers took to the field knowing it could have been them In the final few minutes before stepping into the arena once more, heading out for his 199th Osasuna match on Saturday evening, the man who has scored more first division goals than anyone in their history stopped his teammates for a moment and told them what it meant to wear the shirt. “This is very important,” Ante Budimir began as the dressing room, their sanctuary, fell silent around him. “We don’t have this shirt today for the sake of it. He was not chosen, and nor are we. It could have happened to anyone, anyone. Let us go knowing that we’re grateful to be on the pitch: playing, watching, warming up, sitting on the bench, whatever it may be. Boys, we were not chosen: not us, not him. Let us go, gratefully. Without thought. We have a grand day before us.” With that, Osasuna’s players turned left out of the room, where they were joined in the tunnel by footballers from Athletic Club, rivals from the north, and together they went out past the little shrine of Saint Fermin on to the field. They carried white lilies and all wore the same white shirts with a No 9 on the back, a black ribbon and the name of Jesús de Miguel, the Tenerife striker who died after a collision on the pitch five days earlier at the age of 30. At almost exactly the same time, 2,000km away to the west, Tenerife’s squad were walking out at the Heliodoro Rodríguez López in Santa Cruz. They did not have anyone alongside them, wore black suits not white shirts and did not have a game to play either, not this week. Continue reading...

item.description: Delap’s talents resurface in style, Gómez delights Brighton with more fireworks, and hair-pulling confusion at Everton It would have been very easy for Oliver Glasner to lose patience with Liam Delap. The forward is still only 23, yet the days when he was rattling in 12 in a Premier League season for Ipswich have come to seem a very long time ago (and his six games for Manchester City even longer). A season at Chelsea had left him bereft of confidence, an odd mix of diffidence and overaggression, devoid of composure in the box, arms flailing like a broken windmill. But the old gifts have not left him. Both goals on Saturday were the result of great muscular surges and if the first finish seemed essentially about hitting the ball as hard as possible on target, the second was a precise – and still powerful – finish in off the far post. After games such as this it’s possible to imagine him as England’s long-term replacement for Harry Kane. item.title: Rise of the ‘schooligans’: how a wave of antisocial behaviour threatens non-league football
item.description: Teenage ultras are increasingly causing disorder and communities fear it will not be long before it becomes something more dangerous It is five past three on Saturday afternoon and the teenage ultras of Hednesford Town are running late. They have arrived in Chester for their team’s National League North fixture and have hailed taxis, determined to make their presence felt at the ground. But word appears to have got out about their arrival. As one car turns away from the city’s charming half-timbered houses and into narrow residential streets, half a dozen local youths appear, haring round the corner in balaclavas. They try to attack the cab and chase after it as it pulls away. The smell of pyro is everywhere. As the taxi finally gets clear, the Chester gang stops in the middle of the road, shouting and gesticulating. One lad, no older than 16, pulls a long blade from inside his trousers and brandishes it. The incident ended there and no one was hurt, though a police investigation has been launched. The match went off without trouble too and the Hednesford gang – known at home as the “schooligans” – were escorted safely back to the station by Cheshire police. It was just another weekend in English non-league football, where a wave of antisocial behaviour is causing concern and leading the UK Football Policing Unit (UKFPU) to declare it its “most important” priority. As the disorder continues, a question remains: how long will it be before teenage trouble-making becomes something more dangerous? Continue reading...

item.title: Billions in revenue proves Fifa right on the World Cup – but only on things it cares about
item.description: The 2026 edition of the tournament brought in untold amounts of money to Gianni Infantino’s governing body The total hasn’t entirely stopped rising yet, still clicking away towards a final tally. Still, Fifa has already announced that it surpassed its own lofty revenue projections for the 2026 World Cup, bringing in $15bn, significantly more than anticipated. It appears that a third of that total – $5bn – came from ticket sales and hospitality alone, per reporting from the Times . That would mean direct income from the matchgoing fans came in five times as high in the United States, Canada and Mexico as it did at the last World Cup, in Qatar in 2022, when the total stood at $929m. While 2026’s expanded World Cup added 40 games to the schedule, the takings nevertheless went from an average of about $14.5m per match to about $48m. Continue reading...

item.title: Choke of the century? Chengdu collapse sets up thrilling Chinese Super League climax
item.description: John Aloisi’s players need a point on the final day to seal their maiden title – but their form has dropped off a cliff With four games of the Chinese Super League to go, Chengdu Rongcheng needed just a point to clinch their first title. With one game to go, they still need a point. What was a formality has become a formidable task. The biggest bottle job in Asian football history is very much on and it would be as popular as it would be dramatic. The coach of the Sichuan club, the former Portsmouth and Coventry striker John Aloisi, has seen a 12-point lead over Dalian Yingbo cut to just three before Sunday’s showdowns. Whatever happens, this is a positive and thrilling end to a season that started negatively – literally – with nine of the 16 top-tier clubs kicking off on minus points. Continue reading...

item.title: Rampant Salford hint that Beckham’s lofty ambitions are not a pipe dream
item.description: The aim of reaching the Championship looks more realistic for a Manchester club in the shadow of City and United After seven seasons in League Two, Salford City are finally threatening to match the hype brought by their high-profile owners. First it was the Class of ’92 who guided them up through the non-league system into the fourth tier but failed to progress any further. Gary Neville and David Beckham remain, part of a new group that took over in May 2025, with this year beginning to look transformational after securing an eighth straight win, against Exeter, to put them five points clear at the top. The budget has increased, allowing the club to sign a number of players who will feel they are above League Two standard. Striker Macaulay Langstaff arrived from Millwall; the last time he played at this level, he scored 28 league goals in a season for Notts County. Match-winner Will Aimson spent the past two seasons in the division above with Wigan and has dropped down because of Salford’s project. Continue reading...

item.title: How can playing for Manchester City fit into Marc Guéhi’s moral universe? | Barney Ronay
item.description: Club’s predicament raises interesting questions about principles, both for individuals and the Premier League I felt unbelievably ponderous. My head was made of Aztec stone. item.title: A phone-free Yellow Wall: are Dortmund urging fans to be present or policing them?
item.description: It makes sense that sports teams want to keep influencers out of their games. The battle some clubs are waging with their fans, however, is a different dilemma By all appearances, things on the Yellow Wall seemed as they always had been. The stadium announcer hollered out the first names of Borussia Dortmund’s starting lineup and the supporters responded with their last names, tens of thousands of voices bellowing as one. Dozens of black and yellow flags waved over Europe’s largest standing terrace, a mass of faces fixed on the field beneath them. And then Signal Iduna Park, sold out with 81,365 fans, roared when Max Beier’s lone goal led Dortmund to victory over Eintracht Frankfurt last Saturday, putting the home side even on points with Bayern Munich atop the Bundesliga standings. item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: Ian Holloway’s circus: why the manager’s antics are no laughing matter for fans
item.description: Swindon manager has a history of viral outbursts but fans want a united club and manager they can support In Ian Holloway’s often madcap managerial orbit, this was simply the latest in a steady succession of eccentric outbursts. Eyes bulging as he spoke, he boomed the letter “D” and promptly stabbed himself in the chest with an imaginary dagger. Next came the letter “M” alongside a blow from another invisible knife. Finally, a “W” followed by a jab to the heart. “Dead. Man. Walking,” he declared, pausing for effect between words and briefly falling into an Oscar-worthy zombie stupor. “That’s how it feels.” To an offbeat press conference genre containing seagulls following trawlers and self-proclaimed special ones, it was a crazy new entry worthy of its subsequent viral nature. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
